subject: The fitted-bedroom journey from measure to installation
hook: Sliding or hinged? Your bedroom floor decides.
ig:
Sliding or hinged? Your bedroom floor usually decides before you do.

This is one of the first questions we look at when we measure for fitted wardrobes, because it changes the whole layout.

Sliding doors need no swing space. In a narrow room where the bed sits close to the wardrobe wall, they are often the only practical option. The catch: the doors overlap, so you are only ever looking into part of the wardrobe at once.

Hinged doors open fully, so you can see every rail and shelf together and plan the interior more freely. They need clear floor in front of them, roughly the width of each door.

Which would work in your room, and how much space is there between your bed and the wardrobe wall? Comment A or B with the gap and we will tell you what we would look at.
fb:
A quick one for your Sunday: sliding or hinged wardrobe doors?

Sliding doors save floor space, which is a big help in smaller bedrooms, but you only see part of the wardrobe open at once. Hinged doors give you the full view inside, but they need room in front to swing.

Which would you go for, and why? If you're not sure, tell us roughly how much space you've got between the bed and the wardrobe wall and we'll give you our honest take. Both options are here:
